title: xiom fmt
concept: `xiom fmt` automatically formats XIOM source code to the canonical style — no tabs-vs-spaces debates, no manual alignment.
why: Code formatting disagreements waste team time. `xiom fmt` ends the debate by providing one authoritative style that everyone's code conforms to automatically.
theory:
## Automatic Code Formatting

```sh
# Format a single file
xiom fmt src/main.xi

# Format all files in a directory
xiom fmt src/

# Check if code is formatted (CI mode)
xiom fmt --check src/

# Format with specific options
xiom fmt --indent 4 --max-width 100 src/
```

### What xiom fmt Controls

- **Indentation**: 4 spaces by default (configurable)
- **Line width**: 100 characters max, wraps at operator boundaries
- **Brace style**: same-line opening brace
- **Spacing**: consistent around operators, commas, and colons
- **Blank lines**: single blank line between functions, none at file end
- **Import ordering**: alphabetically sorted, grouped by source

### Before and After

```xiom
// Before (manually formatted)
fn foo(x:Int,y:Int)->Int{
if x>y{return x;}return y;
}

// After xiom fmt
fn foo(x: Int, y: Int) -> Int {
  if x > y { return x; }
  return y;
}
```

### CI Integration

```sh
# Fail CI if code isn't formatted
xiom fmt --check src/ || exit 1
```

### Configuration

```toml
# xiomfmt.toml
indent_width = 4
max_width = 100
use_tabs = false
```

Place this in your project root to override defaults.
syntax_ref:
xiom fmt <file|dir>          # format code
xiom fmt --check <dir>        # verify formatting (CI)
xiom fmt --indent 2 <file>    # custom indent
tips: Run `xiom fmt` before every commit — integrate it as a pre-commit hook
Use `--check` in CI to ensure all code is consistently formatted
Configure indent width once in xiomfmt.toml — the whole team uses it
Auto-formatting saves more time than you think — never manually align code again
common_mistakes: Forgetting to run fmt before committing — causes unnecessary diff noise
Configuring fmt per-file instead of at the project level
Not adding xiomfmt.toml to version control — different team members get different formatting
